haiku-low.q1: Keys load at process startup via load(). /healthz returns non-200 until load succeeds, so the instance is not ready before keys are loaded.
haiku-low.q2: It makes 4 attempts, 2 seconds apart. If all fail, it exits non-zero, never becomes ready and gets no traffic. Running pods keep serving and the rollout halts.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes refresh() re-reads the three keys and updates memory if a newer version exists. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning naming the secret, and keeps serving.
haiku-low.q4: Key values live only in process memory. They must never be written to disk, environment variables or logs. Logs may include version ids.
haiku-low.q5: orders-api-prod has read-only access to orders-api/prod/*. Only the security on-call group can write prod secrets. Engineers cannot read prod values.
haiku-low.q6: Keys stay in git history and in old images, so removing them from the file does not help. They become harmless when rotated at providers and revoked after step 9.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider client calls secrets.get(name) on every request instead of copying the key at build time, so a refreshed value is used without restart.
haiku-low.q8: After writing the new version, wait at least one 5-minute refresh cycle, then confirm all 4 pods report the new version id in secret_versions. Revoke only after that.
haiku-low.q9: 1 set access; 2 copy keys into store; 3 to 6 as one change set (read from store, readiness, remove keys from file); 7 point make run at dev; 8 deploy and verify; 9 rotate and revoke at providers.
haiku-low.q10: From orders-api/dev/* sandbox keys, using engineers' dev access, held in memory only. Local runs never use prod keys.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The plan only says a missing dev key makes the local app fail at load with a clear error.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided a rotation schedule, and the plan sets no cadence.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first: load() runs at process start, and /healthz returns non-200 until load() has succeeded, so the pod gets no traffic until keys are loaded.
sonnet.q2: load() tries once, then retries 3 more times (2 s apart); if all fail the process exits non-zero (or stays not-ready), never becomes ready, and gets no traffic. The rollout halts and the old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: Every 5 minutes refresh() re-reads the three keys; if the store has a newer version, memory is updated. If the read fails, the app keeps its last good value, logs a warning naming the failed secret, and keeps serving.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory. They must never be written to disk, environment variables, or logs (version ids may appear in logs and /healthz).
sonnet.q5: Read prod: only the orders-api-prod service identity (read-only on orders-api/prod/*). Engineers cannot read prod. Write prod: only the security on-call group.
sonnet.q6: Old git history and old images still contain the leaked keys. The keys are made harmless by rotating them at the providers (new key) and revoking the old keys (step 9).
sonnet.q7: Each provider client (PaymentsClient, EmailClient, GeocodingClient) calls secrets.get(name) on every request instead of copying the key at build time, so refreshed values take effect without a restart.
sonnet.q8: After writing the new version and waiting at least one 5-minute refresh cycle, check each of the 4 pods directly via /healthz; every pod's secret_versions must show the new version id. Only then revoke the old key.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set up store access; 2) create secrets (copy keys in); 3-5) write secrets.py, switch clients to secrets.get(), update /healthz; 6) remove api_key from config file and add CI check (steps 3-6 merge and deploy together); 7) make run to dev; 8) deploy and verify; 9) rotate keys and revoke old ones; 10) update deploy.md.
sonnet.q10: From the secret store's sandbox keys under orders-api/dev/* (make run sets APP_ENV=dev), read using the engineer's own dev access. It must never fall back to prod keys.
sonnet.q12: Undecided. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate on a schedule; the plan sets no cadence, and a decision is needed before the migration is called finished.
